human_text:
This is the "SLHE Game Coding Class" / "Game development class curriculum" project — a multi-engine (8 engines) game dev curriculum with an established set of conventions (Lesson Production Standards doc, CLAUDE.md/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md-style context files, per-lesson asset folders, etc.), similar in spirit to another project I work with called Backup Dedupe.

Before doing anything else:
1. Find and read whatever project context/rules files exist here (look for things like CLAUDE.md, PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, a Lesson Production Standards doc, RobertsToDo-style files, or similar) to understand the established folder structure, naming conventions, and asset-file conventions used across lessons.
2. Locate Lesson 6's folder and its assets subfolder specifically. Check how other lessons' asset folders are structured and named (e.g. look at Lesson 5 or Lesson 7 for the pattern) so the new files land in the right place with the right naming convention.
3. IMPORTANT: grep/search the existing Lesson 6 content (handouts, keys, build scripts, GDD) for any already-referenced filenames for a "game start" / "announcement" sound or a "victory" / "end of game" sound — placeholder assets are sometimes already named in the lesson content before the actual file exists (similar to how "explosion_placeholder.png" was already referenced before being created). If such expected filenames exist, use them exactly so the new audio actually gets picked up by existing lesson content. If nothing is referenced yet, choose sensible, conventional names consistent with the project's existing asset naming style.

Then, generate two sound effects in an authentic 80s arcade retro space-shooter style, synthesized directly (procedural audio via ffmpeg/sox — sine/square/saw waves, simple envelopes, arpeggios — no external AI audio service is available, so keep it in that achievable "chiptune" register rather than attempting realistic/recorded-style audio):

1. Start-of-game "announcement" sound — think classic arcade attract-mode fanfare/jingle, the kind of short synth stinger that plays when a game boots up or a new round starts (e.g. a rising square-wave arpeggio, maybe with a brief noise-based "power-up" sweep).
2. End-of-game victory sound — a triumphant ascending major-key 8-bit fanfare/jingle, classic "you win" arcade sound.

Keep both short (a few seconds), in a common format matching whatever convention the project already uses for audio assets (check existing audio files if any exist elsewhere in the project for format/sample-rate conventions — likely .wav or .mp3). Verify the generated files aren't corrupt (ffprobe check) and that they actually sound like reasonable retro chiptune stingers, not just raw tones, before finalizing.

Save both files into Lesson 6's assets folder. Update whatever project context/status files are conventionally updated after this kind of work (following the same pattern as other completed work in this project), and report back a concise summary: exact file paths, naming used, and how they fit (or didn't) an existing placeholder reference.
assistant_text:
Good, all tools available. Let me check the existing audio format and search Lesson 6 content plus the Standards doc.

Sounds are valid but slightly short for a "fanfare" feel — let me extend both a bit for a fuller arcade-jingle length.

No CLAUDE.md/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md exists in this project (unlike Backup Dedupe) — I searched thoroughly and confirmed there's no such context-file convention here. The closest equivalent, `Lessons/Lesson 00 - Standards/Lesson_Production_Standards.docx`, gave me the actual rules I needed: asset folders are `Lessons/Lesson NN.../Assets/`, files use lowercase `sfx_<action>.wav` naming (matching `sfx_shoot.wav`, `sfx_hit.wav` from Lessons 3–4), and any sound referenced-but-not-yet-supplied must be bundled before shipping (Rule 3, self-containment).

Lesson 6 had no Assets folder yet, but two of its eight Teacher's Keys (001 Game Creator and Unreal) already reference `Play Sound(sfx_win.wav)` for the victory moment — exactly the "placeholder referenced before the file exists" pattern you described. I used that exact filename. No "game start" sound was referenced anywhere in Lesson 6, so I named it `sfx_start.wav` to match the project's `sfx_<verb>` convention.

Both were synthesized procedurally in Python/numpy (square-wave arpeggios, a chirp sweep, ADSR envelopes, a layered major chord) — no external audio service, matching the existing files' mono/44.1kHz/16-bit PCM WAV format:

- `sfx_start.wav` (1.48s) — 3-note rising arpeggio → power-up chirp sweep with noise sizzle → punchy landing hit
- `sfx_win.wav` (2.30s) — 6-note ascending C-major arpeggio (two octaves) into a held, shimmering major chord

Both verified with ffprobe (valid PCM, correct duration/format) and spectral analysis confirming actual pitch movement over time (not flat tones) and proper envelope dynamics, no clipping.

Saved to: `D:\SLHE Programming 2026\Lessons\Lesson 06 - Programming Basics V\Assets\sfx_start.wav` and `...\sfx_win.wav`

One thing worth flagging: Lesson 6's Prep Checklist currently says "No new assets this week," which is now slightly stale since `sfx_win.wav` is bundled. I didn't edit that formal deliverable on my own — let me know if you'd like me to update it.
